A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed new tools for the study of the linearized theory for thin elastic shells.
we have shown the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the Koiter model under hypotheses on regularity that are much weaker than those required in previous work.
we have developed a theory for the Koiter shell model for linearly isotropic, homogeneous elastic shells whose midsurface can have charts whose second derivatives are only piecewise smooth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Koiter shell model can be used to model a large class of thin shells, including those with discontinuous midsurfaces.
the Koiter shell model is well posed for shells whose midsurface can have charts with piecewise smooth second derivatives.
the linear Koiter shell model is well posed for shells that have little regularity.
